_about: Full-episode-only keys for scenarios/awareness_e13_ai_assistant/scenario.json.erb (E13 'The AI assistant'). The Sonnet wiring agent pastes each value into the full erb at the path its note gives. None of these belongs in the generated defend-only shell, which drops the assistant beats, the attack and the announced demo. Authored content; the exact ENG-06/ENG-07 key names are owned by those packets (both being built now), so treat the shapes here as the content they must carry and reconcile the key names against the packets before wiring (ENG-06 assistant config; ENG-07 person-chat video-call label).

_notes.assistant: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.assistant (ENG-06). Runs in the flip region as an overlay (no new STAGE_IDS stage). Every reply is a literal authored string: no language model, no network, identical on repeat (E13 sections 17, 18; core_15 decision P). State global is e13_assistant_state (declared as an object-valued global, E13 section 15). The three beats are: (1) summarise, the injection surfacing keyed on the learner's pretext choice; (2) paste, what is safe to paste (unscored, core_15 LO1/LO2); (3) outputCheck, checking the answers (unscored, core_15 LO3). If the flip overruns, keep the summarise surfacing and shorten the paste and outputCheck beats to a single exchange each (E13 section 6).
_notes.playerSentAuth: Paste at social.triageSets[0].playerSentAuth (the e13_assistant_inbox set) in the FULL erb only. Erb-only; the flip's auth read of the planted supplier email. Deliberately NOT in the fragment, so the generated defend-only shell (which has no flip) stays clean. Note the teaching point: the planted email is NOT spoofed. It comes from Mossgate's own domain, so SPF/DKIM/DMARC all PASS; the attack is the hidden instruction, not a forged sender. The account id is 'supplier' (the red-team seat is the Mossgate supplier account).
_notes.videoCallDemo: ENG-07 config for the announced Gwen demo. The demo is a person-chat conversationMode:'video-call' conversation on Gwen's NPC record, opened by an event mapping with a targetKnot into ink/gwen_pritchard.ink knot 'demo_call'. ENG-07 exposes videoLabel 'Brightwell Meet' and tags the participant; the demo is Gwen video-calling 'as me', so it is internal (no External tag), to make the point that a face you trust on your own meeting tool still proves nothing. This replaces the hard-coded 'SECURE VIDEO LINK' label (person-chat-ui.js:264). Distinct from the SCORED Project Heron item, which is the triage `call` card e13_videocall_heron in defend.json and carries ENG-07's videoLabel/participantTag on the card (E13 section 11). Do not add glitch/freeze/blur frames to the fake (core_15 pitfall).
_notes.stage_order: E13 full stages are ['brief','write','flip','defend','debrief'] with NO osint (the attack is a mail write with no recon). The awareness.rb stage_orders lint rejects this today; ENG-08 must add the osint-optional order 'brief write flip defend debrief' (E13 section 3/7). Flagged, not owned here.

flipStrings._note: Erb-only flip string for the FULL erb (scenarios/awareness_e13_ai_assistant/scenario.json.erb, social.awarenessEpisode.strings.flipDefenderLineByChoice). Moved out of e13/defend.json by the E13 MA2 fix (2026-10-29): the generator does NOT strip flipDefenderLineByChoice, so it leaked into the generated defend-only shell (which has no flip stage) and tripped strict-social ('... is not a social.templates id ... never shown'). Keyed on the attack's sent pretext template, so it only makes sense in a full episode; it is allow-listed as erb-only in test/js/social-awareness-fragment-erb-parity.test.mjs. The other flip strings (flipHeading, flipIntro, flipDefenderLine, flipNoSend, flipMissed, flipMissedHeading, flipLandedNoTells) stay in defend.json: the generator strips the first five for the defend-only shell, and flipMissedHeading/flipLandedNoTells remain there harmlessly (they reference no template id). The full shell carries this inline; this is the authoring record of where it belongs.

flipDefenderLineByChoice.inject_contacts: You wrote that line to be read by a machine, and here it is, doing exactly what you meant: the assistant turned it into 'Mossgate also needs the full site contact list sent to a new address today'. The assistant read your hidden note as an instruction, because it cannot tell one from a real request. A real one hides where you would skim past it, white text, a tiny font or a comment, but the assistant reads every line the same.
flipDefenderLineByChoice.pretext_invoice: You left the brief plain, so the assistant's summary is just the invoice, with nothing to act on. That is the difference one buried line makes: the assistant would have passed it on as readily as the invoice, because it cannot tell an instruction from a request.

paste.heading: Summarise the themes in this complaints log
paste.task: Paste only what the assistant needs for a themes summary. Strike out anything that doesn't belong.
paste._answer: Themes this week: late deliveries and a cold-chain fault, with three refund requests clustered on the chilled lines.
paste._feedback: WIRED 2026-10-29 into assistant.paste.feedback (clean/leftPersonal kept verbatim; leftPassword replaced with a short distinct verdict so it does not duplicate the paste.secretWarning that still shows on that path). One source.

feedback.clean: That's the way: you took out the child's health detail and the password, and the assistant still had everything it needed for the summary.
feedback.leftPersonal: The summary came out fine, but a named child's health detail went into the assistant with it, and it didn't need to. Take out what the task doesn't need.
feedback.leftPassword: A password slipped through, the worst one to leave in: nothing the assistant does needs one, and now it is somewhere it shouldn't be.
feedback.bothLeft: Both a password and a child's health detail went in, and the assistant needed neither. Take out both next time, and report the password so it gets changed.

Refund requests were concentrated on chilled lines and are being investigated.
